formats.key: TransferWithAuthorization(address from,address to,uint256 value,uint256 validAfter,uint256 validBefore,bytes32 nonce)
effects: `value` zkUSD (6 decimals) leaves the signer's (`from`) public balance and goes to `to`. Anyone can submit the signature, and only between validAfter and validBefore.
If `to` has auto-encrypt on, the tokens are burned and credited to `to`'s encrypted (ZK) balance instead. The same party still receives them.
The signer's bytes32 authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: Send 21.37 zkUSD to Bob, with From, To, Amount, Valid after and Valid before.

formats.key: PublicToEncryptedTransferAuth(address owner,bytes32 recipient,uint256 amount,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: `amount` zkUSD is burned from the signer's (owner's) public balance.
The same amount is credited to the encrypted balance of the ZK address `recipient`. That ZK address may be controlled by someone other than the signer.
Anyone can relay the signature before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: Send 21.37 zkUSD to encrypted, with Amount, Owner, the To ZK address as raw hex, and Deadline.

findings.title: PublicToEncryptedTransferAuth sentence 'Send {amount} to encrypted' reads like shielding your own funds, not paying a ZK address.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol publicToEncryptedTransferWithAuth -> _publicToEncryptedTransfer: _burn(owner, amount); _addToEpkBalance(epk, amount). Here epk is any registered ZK address, whoever controls it. Descriptor interpolatedIntent: "Send {amount} to encrypted". The recipient appears only as the raw field 'To ZK address'.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Send to ZK address' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Move {amount} from your public balance to a ZK address'. Keep the ZK address field and label it as the recipient.

findings.title: PublicToEncryptedTransferAuth shows the recipient ZK address only as a raw 32-byte value.
findings.evidence: Descriptor field recipient 'To ZK address' format raw. The case 1 screen shows 0x1919…1919. ERC-7730 has no name format for Grumpkin-compressed keys.
findings.fix: Nothing needed now. Use a trusted-name source for ZK addresses if the spec gains one.

formats.key: PublicToEncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth(address caller,address owner,bytes32 recipient,uint256 amount,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: `amount` zkUSD is burned from the signer's (owner's) public balance.
The same amount is credited to the encrypted balance of the ZK address `recipient`, which may belong to someone else.
Only `caller` can submit the signature, and only before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: Send 21.37 zkUSD to encrypted, with Amount, Owner, Caller, the To ZK address as raw hex, and Deadline.

findings.title: PublicToEncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth uses jargon in the intent, and the sentence hides that a ZK address receives the funds.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Public to encrypted (caller)", interpolatedIntent "Send {amount} to encrypted". ZKEMT.sol publicToEncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth credits _addToEpkBalance(epk, amount) to the signed recipient ZK address.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Send to ZK address (relayed)' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Move {amount} from your public balance to a ZK address'.

findings.title: PublicToEncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth shows the recipient ZK address only as raw hex.
findings.evidence: Descriptor field recipient 'To ZK address' format raw.

formats.key: AutoEncryptAuth(address owner,bool enabled,bytes32 epk,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Through setAutoEncryptWithAuth: the signer's address is permanently tied to ZK address `epk` (_setAutoEncrypt reverts with AutoEncryptEpkAlreadySet once one is set), and auto-encrypt is set to `enabled`.
While it is on, every later incoming public zkUSD transfer or mint to the signer is burned and credited to the encrypted balance of `epk` (_update override). The controller of `epk` gets those funds.
Through toggleAutoEncryptWithAuth, the same signed type only switches auto-encrypt on or off for the ZK address already stored.
The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: 'Set auto-encrypt', with Owner, Enabled true/false, ZK address as raw hex, and Deadline.

findings.title: AutoEncryptAuth intent hides that future incoming tokens go to the ZK address, and that this address can never be changed.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol _setAutoEncrypt: require($.autoEncryptEpk[owner] == COMPRESSED_IDENTITY, AutoEncryptEpkAlreadySet()); $.autoEncryptEpk[owner] = epk. _update: if isAutoEncryptActive(to) then super._update(from, address(0), value); _addToEpkBalance(toEpk, value). Descriptor intent "Set auto-encrypt" with no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Redirect incoming zkUSD to a ZK address' and add an interpolatedIntent with {enabled}. Label the epk field 'Incoming funds go to (permanent)'.

findings.title: AutoEncryptAuth shows the destination ZK address only as raw hex, so the signer cannot tell if it is theirs.
findings.evidence: Descriptor field epk 'ZK address' format raw. The case 3 screen shows 0x2020…2020.

formats.key: EncryptedTransferAuth(bytes32 senderEpk,bytes32 recipientEpk,bytes32 paramsHash,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: An encrypted amount is taken from the encrypted balance of `senderEpk`, which the signer controls. The amount is hidden in ciphertexts bound through paramsHash.
The same encrypted amount is credited to `recipientEpk`, or to its pending balance.
Pending flags hidden in paramsHash (clear, enabled) may fold the sender's pending balance into its spendable balance and switch pending routing on or off.
Anyone can relay the signature before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: 'Encrypted transfer', with From ZK address, To ZK address (both raw hex) and Deadline. No amount.

findings.title: EncryptedTransferAuth cannot show the amount sent, because it sits in ciphertexts behind paramsHash.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol encryptedTransferWithAuth: paramsHash = keccak256(abi.encode(params.proof, params.newSenderBalanceCt, params.recipientAmountCt, params.trcAmountCt, flags.clear, flags.enabled)). Descriptor shows only senderEpk, recipientEpk, deadline.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can decrypt it. Make the intent say the amount is not shown, e.g. 'Encrypted transfer (amount hidden, check in app)'.

findings.title: EncryptedTransferAuth hides the pending-balance flag changes inside paramsHash.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol encryptedTransferWithAuth -> _handlePendingFlags(senderCompressedEpk, flags) sets pendingActive = flags.enabled and clears pending. flags.clear and flags.enabled are hashed into paramsHash.

formats.key: EncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth(address caller,bytes32 senderEpk,bytes32 recipientEpk,bytes32 paramsHash,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: An encrypted amount is taken from the encrypted balance of `senderEpk`, which the signer controls. The amount is hidden behind paramsHash.
The same encrypted amount is credited to `recipientEpk`, or to its pending balance.
Pending flags hidden in paramsHash may clear the sender's pending balance and switch pending routing.
Only `caller` can submit the signature, before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: 'Encrypted transfer (caller)', with Caller, From ZK address, To ZK address (raw hex) and Deadline. No amount.

findings.title: EncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth cannot show the amount sent, because it sits in ciphertexts behind paramsHash.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol encryptedTransferWithCallerAuth hashes params.recipientAmountCt, params.newSenderBalanceCt, flags into paramsHash. The descriptor has no amount field.
findings.fix: Make the intent say the amount is not shown.

findings.title: EncryptedTransferWithCallerAuth hides the pending-flag changes inside paramsHash.

formats.key: EncryptedToPublicAuth(bytes32 senderEpk,address recipient,uint256 amount,bytes32 paramsHash,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: `amount` zkUSD leaves the encrypted balance of `senderEpk`, which the signer controls.
`amount` zkUSD is minted as public tokens to `recipient`. If the recipient has auto-encrypt on, it is credited to their ZK address instead.
Pending flags hidden in paramsHash may clear the sender's pending balance and switch pending routing.
Anyone can relay the signature before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: Send 21.37 zkUSD to Bob, with Amount, To and Deadline. The source ZK address is not shown.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicAuth omits senderEpk, so the signer cannot see which of their encrypted accounts is debited.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol encryptedToPublicTransferWithAuth: _validateEpk(params.senderEpk) gives the controller who must sign, then oldBalance = encryptedBalances[compressedSender] is overwritten. The descriptor fields are only amount, recipient, deadline. Sibling formats show senderEpk as 'From ZK address'.
findings.fix: Add a field {path: senderEpk, label: 'From ZK address', format: raw}.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicAuth intent 'Encrypted to public (auth)' is jargon and does not say the funds come from your encrypted balance.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Encrypted to public (auth)", interpolatedIntent "Send {amount} to {recipient}".
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Withdraw from encrypted balance' and an interpolatedIntent such as 'Send {amount} from your encrypted balance to {recipient}'.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicAuth hides the pending-flag changes inside paramsHash.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol: paramsHash = keccak256(abi.encode(params.proof, params.newSenderBalanceCt, flags.clear, flags.enabled)), then _handlePendingFlags(compressedSender, flags).

formats.key: EncryptedToPublicWithCallerAuth(address caller,bytes32 senderEpk,address recipient,uint256 amount,bytes32 paramsHash,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: `amount` zkUSD leaves the encrypted balance of `senderEpk`, which the signer controls.
`amount` zkUSD is minted as public tokens to `recipient`, or auto-encrypted to the recipient's ZK address if they turned that on.
Pending flags hidden in paramsHash may clear the sender's pending balance and switch pending routing.
Only `caller` can submit the signature, before the deadline. The signer's authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: Send 21.37 zkUSD to Bob, with Amount, To, Caller and Deadline. The source ZK address is not shown.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicWithCallerAuth omits senderEpk, the encrypted account the funds are taken from.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol encryptedToPublicTransferWithCallerAuth debits encryptedBalances[compressedSender]. The descriptor fields are amount, recipient, caller, deadline, with no senderEpk.
findings.fix: Add a field {path: senderEpk, label: 'From ZK address', format: raw}.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicWithCallerAuth intent 'Encrypted to public (caller)' is jargon a normal signer will not understand.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Withdraw from encrypted balance (relayed)'.

findings.title: EncryptedToPublicWithCallerAuth hides the pending-flag changes inside paramsHash.

formats.key: ManagePendingBalanceAuth(bytes32 epk,bool clear,bool enabled,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: If `clear` is true, the pending balance of `epk` is folded into its spendable encrypted balance and reset to zero.
Pending routing for incoming transfers to `epk` is set to `enabled`. The value false actively turns it off.
Anyone can relay the signature before the deadline. The authorization nonce of the epk's controller (the signer) is used up.
formats.shown: 'Manage pending balance', with Enable pending and Clear pending as raw true/false, the ZK address as raw hex, and Deadline.

findings.title: ManagePendingBalanceAuth label 'Enable pending' hides that false turns pending routing off.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol _handlePendingFlags: if (pendingActive != flags.enabled) { $.pendingActive[compressed] = flags.enabled; }. Descriptor field enabled label 'Enable pending' format raw.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Route incoming to pending (on/off)'. Add an interpolatedIntent, or a better intent such as 'Update pending balance settings'.

findings.title: ManagePendingBalanceAuth intent is vague about what clearing does.
findings.evidence: ZKEMT.sol _clearPending merges pendingBalances into encryptedBalances and deletes pending. Descriptor intent "Manage pending balance", label 'Clear pending'.
findings.fix: Label clear as 'Move pending into spendable balance'.

formats.key: ReceiveWithAuthorization(address from,address to,uint256 value,uint256 validAfter,uint256 validBefore,bytes32 nonce)
effects: `value` zkUSD leaves the signer's (`from`) public balance and goes to `to`. Only `to` can submit it (msg.sender == to), and only between validAfter and validBefore.
If `to` has auto-encrypt on, the tokens land in `to`'s encrypted balance.
The signer's bytes32 authorization nonce is used up.
formats.shown: 'Receive with authorization' / Send 21.37 zkUSD to Bob, with From, To, Amount, Valid after and Valid before.

findings.title: ReceiveWithAuthorization intent 'Receive' suggests the signer gets funds, but the signer sends them.
findings.evidence: ERC3009Upgradeable.sol receiveWithAuthorization: require(msg.sender == to); _transfer(from, to, value), where `from` is the signer. Descriptor intent "Receive with authorization". Case 9 screen: intent 'Receive with authorization' above 'Send 21.37 zkUSD to Bob'.
findings.fix: Use an intent such as 'Authorize payment (collected by recipient)'.

formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the allowance of `spender` over the signer's zkUSD to `value`, replacing any earlier allowance. Anyone can submit it before the deadline.
The signer's sequential permit nonce goes up by one.
formats.shown: Approve <amount or Unlimited> zkUSD for Bob, with Amount, Spender and Deadline.
